output.name: Hilun — the Windward Gull
output.myth: Hilun carried word between the islands and Vel. She flew so close to the Gale that Tavo grew fond of her, and fond is a dangerous thing in a god. One day he laughed and tore the feathers from one wing, the way he tears a sail. Hilun fell, and the Gulls cried for three days. Ennu the Kite-Wright sewed her a new wing from old sailcloth and waxed thread. It did not fly as well as the first, but it flew. Ennu's hands already knew the work; he had sat three nights over the Mended Gull with the same cloth and whalebone. Hilun went up on the cloth wing and hung her spread body on the Windward edge, where the wind is loudest. Sekra, who fell back from the frost, hangs a hand-span below her to the south, and Hilun does not look down. Fishermen's wives say that when the gale is coming Hilun leans a little, and that is the sign to take the nets in. Tavo still laughs when he passes her, but he goes around.
output.finding: Find Hevalu, the Gull Let Go, and look a hand-span north-west of it, where the Windward Gull hangs on the edge of the sky.
